title: The inclusion of condensed rings $\underline{\mathcal O}_E\to\underline E$
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime and $E\subseteq\Qlb$ a finite extension of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. The
inclusion $\cO_E\hookrightarrow E$ is a continuous ring map, so it induces a morphism of
condensed rings $\underline{\cO}_E\to\underline E$, $f\mapsto f$ on
$C(S,\cO_E)\to C(S,E)$ [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. Its underlying morphism of condensed
abelian groups is a morphism of ring objects of $\Sh(*_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$
[sk-def-sfb-ring-object].

proof.text: Because $E$ is an embedded subfield of $\Qlb$, [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] gives its restricted topology and the condensed rings $\underline E$ and $\underline{\cO}_E$, where $\cO_E=\{x\in E:|x|\le1\}$. Its final clause states that postcomposition with the continuous inclusion $i:\cO_E\hookrightarrow E$ gives a morphism of condensed rings $\underline{\cO}_E\to\underline E$. On each profinite $S$ this sends $a$ to $i\circ a$, displayed as $f\mapsto f$ after identifying an element of $\cO_E$ with its image in $E$. For a restriction along $u:S'\to S$, $i\circ(a\circ u)=(i\circ a)\circ u$. The section maps preserve addition, multiplication, zero and unit because $i$ is a ring homomorphism and the operations are pointwise. The underlying abelian sheaf map is therefore a morphism of ring objects of $\Sh(*_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$ by clause 3 of [sk-def-sfb-ring-object].
